# Libraries and path

```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(mc2d)
library(brms)
library(loo)
library(MASS)
library(gsl)
library(patchwork)

n_variability <- ndvar(10000)
n_uncertainty <- ndunc(2000)

module1_results_dir <- here("results", "module1_1_initial_contamination")
module2_results_dir <- here("results", "module1_2_thermal_inactivation")
module4_results_dir <- here("results", "module4_sensitivity_analysis")
figure_dir <- here("figures")

dir.create(module1_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(module2_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(module4_results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

This master QMD file connects the full 2D Monte Carlo QMRA pathway across four standard stages:

1. **Module 1: Exposure Assessment:** estimate oyster-level GII prevalence and positive concentration (1.1), apply cooking time-temperature profiles (1.2), and generate 2D exposure dose matrices (1.3).
2. **Module 2: Hazard & Risk Characterization:** evaluate the dose-response model and host susceptibility directly on 2D exposure matrices, and estimate annual U.S. illness burden.
3. **Module 3: Model Diagnostics and Sensitivity Analysis:** conduct numerical simulation diagnostics and comprehensive parameter sensitivity analyses.


# Module 1: Exposure Assessment
## 1.1 Initial Contamination Distribution for Norovirus GII in Oysters

## Purpose

Section 1.1 estimates the distributions governing pre-cook norovirus GII genome
copies per oyster. It uses a two-part hurdle model fitted to Nishida 2003 and
2007:

1. a pooled global Beta conjugate prevalence model. Following Dr. Arie Havelaar's
   recommendation, commercial market prevalence across Nishida et al. (2003, 2007)
   is pooled across all sampling batches ($k_{\text{total}} = 63$ GII-positive oysters out of
   $n_{\text{total}} = 1,703$ total commercial market oysters sampled), yielding a global
   prevalence distribution $p \sim \operatorname{Beta}(64, 1641)$ with a population mean of
   3.75% (95% CrI: 2.90%–4.71%); and
2. a left-censored positive-concentration model selected by comparing pooled
   Gamma and lognormal distributions for genome copies per oyster conditional
   on GII positivity.

The posterior draws from both models create 500 uncertainty scenarios for prevalence
and positive-concentration parameters. Section 1.1 establishes the per-oyster baseline
contamination parameters, while individual oyster variability is simulated downstream in Section 1.3.

## Inputs

```{r module1-inputs}
# GII-positive concentration records from Tables 2 of Nishida 2003 and 2007 (for Concentration Model)
nishida_individual_gii_records <- read_csv(
  here(
    "data", "literature_norovirus_contamination",
    "nishida_individual_gii_records.csv"
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

## Prevalence Model
Under a standard non-informative Beta conjugate prior $\operatorname{Beta}(1, 1)$, the posterior prevalence distribution is:

$$
p \sim \operatorname{Beta}(1 + 63, 1 + 1703 - 63) = \operatorname{Beta}(64, 1641)
$$

This pooled global prevalence distribution yields a population mean of **3.75%** (95% CrI: 2.90%–4.71%), which will be preserved for risk characterization module

```{r module1-prevalence-pooled}
mc2d_prevalence_node <- mcdata(withr::with_seed(
  2026L,
  rbeta(n_uncertainty, shape1 = 64, shape2 = 1641),
    .rng_kind = "Mersenne-Twister", .rng_normal_kind = "Inversion",
    .rng_sample_kind = "Rejection"), type = "U")

nishida_prevalence_posterior_summary <- tibble(
  parameter = "Global Pooled Prevalence (P_prev)",
  mean = mean(mc2d_prevalence_node),
  sd = sd(mc2d_prevalence_node),
  median = median(mc2d_prevalence_node),
  lower_2.5 = quantile(mc2d_prevalence_node, 0.025),
  upper_97.5 = quantile(mc2d_prevalence_node, 0.975)
)

nishida_prevalence_posterior_summary

# Clean visualization of Global Pooled Prevalence Beta(64, 1641) distribution
prevalence_plot_df <- tibble(p_prev = as.numeric(mc2d_prevalence_node))
p_prev_plot <- ggplot(prevalence_plot_df, aes(x = p_prev)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 40, fill = "#4E79A7", alpha = 0.7, color = "white") +
  geom_density(color = "#2B5C8F", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(as.numeric(mc2d_prevalence_node)), linetype = "dashed", color = "#D55E00", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(
    x = "HuNoV GII prevalence in market oysters",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
p_prev_plot

ggsave(
  here("figures", "module1_1_global_prevalence_distribution.tiff"),
  p_prev_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```

## Positive-Concentration Model

This model includes only the 63 oysters classified as GII-positive in the
prevalence data. Of these, 22 had quantified concentrations, while 41 were
positive by the qualitative assay but were not quantifiable by the quantitative
assay. These 41 positive observations are represented as left-censored
concentrations, $0 < C \leq 100$ genome copies/oyster. The 1,640 GII-negative
oysters are excluded from the concentration model.

Pooled Gamma and log-normal models are compared by PSIS-LOO on the
original copies/oyster scale. The pooled Gamma candidate is

$$
C\mid C>0 \sim \operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,\kappa/m),
$$

### Candidate Fits and Model Comparison

```{r module1-concentration-model-comparison}
# Left-censored positive-concentration model.
nishida_concentration_data <- nishida_individual_gii_records %>%
  transmute(
    study_id = factor(study_id, levels = c("Nishida_2003", "Nishida_2007")),
    concentration_gc = if_else(
      censoring == "exact",
      concentration_copies_per_oyster,
      upper_copies_per_oyster
    ),
    censor_code = if_else(censoring == "left_censored", -1L, 0L)
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

concentration_formula <- bf(
  concentration_gc | cens(censor_code) ~ 1
)
concentration_shape_priors <- c(
  set_prior("normal(6, 4)", class = "Intercept"),
  set_prior("lognormal(0, 1.5)", class = "shape")
)
concentration_lognormal_priors <- c(
  set_prior("normal(6, 4)", class = "Intercept"),
  set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 2)", class = "sigma")
)

nishida_concentration_gamma_fit <- brm(
  formula = concentration_formula,
  data = nishida_concentration_data,
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  prior = concentration_shape_priors,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  chains = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  cores = 4,
  seed = 1061,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
  file = here("results", "module1_1_initial_contamination", "nishida_concentration_gamma_fit"),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
)

nishida_concentration_lognormal_fit <- brm(
  formula = concentration_formula,
  data = nishida_concentration_data,
  family = lognormal(),
  prior = concentration_lognormal_priors,
  backend = "cmdstanr",
  chains = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  cores = 4,
  seed = 1063,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12),
  file = here("results", "module1_1_initial_contamination", "nishida_concentration_lognormal_fit"),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
)

nishida_concentration_loo <- list(
  pooled_gamma = loo::loo(nishida_concentration_gamma_fit),
  pooled_lognormal = loo::loo(nishida_concentration_lognormal_fit)
)
nishida_concentration_model_comparison <-
  loo::loo_compare(nishida_concentration_loo) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "model") %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  dplyr::select(model, elpd_diff, se_diff, elpd_loo, se_elpd_loo, looic, se_looic)

nishida_concentration_fit <- nishida_concentration_gamma_fit
nishida_concentration_model_comparison
```

### Gamma Posterior and Diagnostics

```{r module1-concentration-posterior}
nishida_concentration_posterior <-
  posterior::as_draws_df(nishida_concentration_fit) %>%
  transmute(
    posterior_draw = .draw,
    chain = .chain,
    iteration = .iteration,
    positive_mean_gc = exp(b_Intercept),
    concentration_gamma_shape = shape,
    concentration_gamma_cv = 1 / sqrt(shape)
  )

nishida_concentration_fit_summary <- summary(nishida_concentration_fit)
nishida_concentration_parameter_summary <- nishida_concentration_posterior %>%
  transmute(
    positive_mean_gc,
    concentration_gamma_shape,
    concentration_gamma_cv,
    positive_median_gc = qgamma(
      0.5,
      shape = concentration_gamma_shape,
      scale = positive_mean_gc / concentration_gamma_shape
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(parameter) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(value),
    sd = sd(value),
    median = median(value),
    lower_2.5 = quantile(value, 0.025),
    upper_97.5 = quantile(value, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

nishida_concentration_fit_summary
nishida_concentration_parameter_summary
```

### Visual Posterior Predictive Check

```{r module1-concentration-ppc}
nishida_concentration_yrep <- withr::with_seed(2030L,
  posterior_predict(nishida_concentration_fit, ndraws = 500),
    .rng_kind = "Mersenne-Twister", .rng_normal_kind = "Inversion",
    .rng_sample_kind = "Rejection")
nishida_concentration_ppc_draws <- tibble(
  draw = rep(seq_len(nrow(nishida_concentration_yrep)),
             each = ncol(nishida_concentration_yrep)),
  study_id = rep(nishida_individual_gii_records$study_id,
                 times = nrow(nishida_concentration_yrep)),
  concentration_gc = as.vector(t(nishida_concentration_yrep))
) %>%
  group_by(draw, study_id) %>%
  summarise(
    `Fraction <100` = mean(concentration_gc < 100),
    `Median quantified GC/oyster` = median(concentration_gc[concentration_gc >= 100]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(draw, study_id), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")

nishida_concentration_ppc_intervals <- nishida_concentration_ppc_draws %>%
  group_by(study_id, metric) %>%
  summarise(
    predicted = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower = quantile(value, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper = quantile(value, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
nishida_concentration_ppc_observed <- nishida_individual_gii_records %>%
  group_by(study_id) %>%
  summarise(
    `Fraction <100` = mean(censoring == "left_censored"),
    `Median quantified GC/oyster` = median(
      concentration_copies_per_oyster[censoring == "exact"]
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-study_id, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")

df_a_pred <- nishida_concentration_ppc_intervals %>% filter(metric == "Fraction <100")
df_a_obs <- nishida_concentration_ppc_observed %>% filter(metric == "Fraction <100")
p_a <- ggplot(df_a_pred, aes(study_id, predicted)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), color = "#4E79A7", linewidth = 1, size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = df_a_obs, aes(y = value), color = "#D55E00", shape = 4, size = 4, stroke = 1.5) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(Nishida_2003 = "2003", Nishida_2007 = "2007")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Year of publication", y = "Left-censored proportion (%)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

df_b_pred <- nishida_concentration_ppc_intervals %>% filter(metric == "Median quantified GC/oyster")
df_b_obs <- nishida_concentration_ppc_observed %>% filter(metric == "Median quantified GC/oyster")
p_b <- ggplot(df_b_pred, aes(study_id, predicted)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), color = "#4E79A7", linewidth = 1, size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = df_b_obs, aes(y = value), color = "#D55E00", shape = 4, size = 4, stroke = 1.5) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(Nishida_2003 = "2003", Nishida_2007 = "2007")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Year of publication", y = "Median quantified concentration (GC/oyster)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

nishida_concentration_pp_check <- p_a + p_b + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
nishida_concentration_pp_check
ggsave(
  here("figures", "module1_1_positive_concentration_ppc.tiff"),
  nishida_concentration_pp_check,
  width = 10,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 600,
  compression = "lzw"
)
```


## 1.2 Thermal Process Modeling

## Purpose

Section 1.2 supplies posterior uncertainty in thermal survival $S(U)$ for each cooking
condition using the Geeraerd model. Pre-cook contamination and serving
variability are not applied here; they are generated in Section 1.3.

## Geeraerd Module Input

```{r}
source(here("scripts", "module1_exposure_assessment_thermal_inactivation_functions.R"))
# Primary Baseline Model: Geeraerd model (includes 100 °C data)
geeraerd_post <- readRDS(
  here("results", "module1_2_thermal_inactivation", "module1_2_geeraerd_thermal_kinetics_posterior.rds")
)

# Sensitivity Analysis Scenario Model: Bayesian Meta-Analysis (Shellfish infectivity kinetics posterior)

  here("results", "module1_2_thermal_inactivation", "module1_2_meta_analysis_thermal_kinetics_posterior.rds")
)

df_comeup_updated <- readRDS(
  here("data", "module1_2_thermal_inactivation", "df_comeup_updated.rds")
)

# Standard cooking scenario time grid (0 to 16 minutes, every 2 min, covering full sensitivity tail)
module2_cooking_time_grid <- seq(0, 16, by = 2)

steam_excel_path <- here("data", "experimental_temperature_profiles", "Steaming small Cumulative.xlsx")
bake_excel_path <- here("data", "experimental_temperature_profiles", "Real Oyster Baking cumulative.xlsx")
```

```{r module2-temperature-profiles-plot}
# Plot internal core temperature profiles
plot_temperature_profiles <- function(steam_path, bake_path) {
  # Extract the profiles using the helper function in module1_exposure_assessment_thermal_inactivation_functions.R
  steam_S <- extract_cooking_profile_min(steam_path, "Small Cumulative", "steaming", "small")
  steam_M <- extract_cooking_profile_min(steam_path, "Medium Cumulative", "steaming", "medium")
  steam_L <- extract_cooking_profile_min(steam_path, "Large Cumulative", "steaming", "large")

  bake_S  <- extract_cooking_profile_min(bake_path, "Small cuml", "baking", "small")
  bake_M  <- extract_cooking_profile_min(bake_path, "Medium cuml", "baking", "medium")
  bake_L  <- extract_cooking_profile_min(bake_path, "Large cuml", "baking", "large")

  all_profiles <- bind_rows(steam_S, steam_M, steam_L, bake_S, bake_M, bake_L) %>%
    mutate(
      size_label = factor(str_to_title(size), levels = c("Small", "Medium", "Large")),
      method_label = str_to_title(method)
    )

  p <- ggplot(all_profiles, aes(x = time, y = temperature, color = size_label, fill = size_label)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = temp_min, ymax = temp_max), alpha = 0.4, color = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
    facet_wrap(~method_label, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 16, by = 2)) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#EAEDED"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Cooking time (min)",
      y = "Internal temperature (°C)",
      color = "Oyster size",
      fill = "Oyster size"
    )
  
  p
}

p_temp <- plot_temperature_profiles(steam_excel_path, bake_excel_path)
p_temp
ggsave(plot = p_temp, filename = here("figures", "module1_2_temperature_profiles.tiff"), width = 10, height = 5)
```

## 1.3 Exposure Dose Calculation

## Purpose

Section 1.3 combines the pre-harvest initial contamination $GC_{\text{precook}}(V, U)$ with the size-stratified thermal survival nodes $S(U)$ from Section 1.2. 

In strict adherence to QMRA principles, **Initial contamination is sampled independently from oyster size**, establishing the baseline population-average exposure. The physical variation of oyster size (**Small, Medium, Large**) operates directly through the size-stratified thermal inactivation kinetics $S_{\text{size}}(U)$ for both **Steaming** and **Baking** scenarios.

Section 1.3 produces 2D per-oyster post-cook residual dose matrices $GC_{\text{postcook, size}}(V, U)$ (in Genome Copies / Infectious Units per oyster). Serving aggregation (6 and 12 oysters) and post-hoc random permutation size mixing are evaluated downstream in Module 2.

## Individual Oyster Pre-Cook & Post-Cook Dose Generation

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Read Global Pooled Prevalence mc2d Uncertainty Node (type = "U", dimension: 2000)
prevalence_selected_u <- c(mc2d_prevalence_node)

# Left-Censored Bayesian Gamma Concentration model draws
concentration_selected <- withr::with_seed(2027L,
  nishida_concentration_posterior[
    sample.int(nrow(nishida_concentration_posterior), n_uncertainty),
  ],
    .rng_kind = "Mersenne-Twister", .rng_normal_kind = "Inversion",
    .rng_sample_kind = "Rejection")

# Generate per-oyster pre-cook contamination matrix
# Biological conversion: Multiply raw qPCR genome copies
# Reference ratio range from Mirmahdi et al. (2025) "Navigating uncertainties in RT-qPCR and plaque assay for infectivity assessment of norovirus":
# 2.5% to 97.5% log10 GC:PFU coverage is [3.39, 4.22] (linear: [2455, 16596]), median is 3.7 log10 (~5012:1).
infectious_dose_precook_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = n_variability, ncol = n_uncertainty)

log10_q_inv_min <- 3.39
log10_q_inv_max <- 4.22 
q_inv_u <- withr::with_seed(2028L,
  10^runif(n_uncertainty, min = log10_q_inv_min, max = log10_q_inv_max),
    .rng_kind = "Mersenne-Twister", .rng_normal_kind = "Inversion",
    .rng_sample_kind = "Rejection")
q_u <- 1 / q_inv_u

infectious_dose_precook_matrix <- withr::with_seed(2029L, {
  for (u in seq_len(n_uncertainty)) {
    p_prev_u <- prevalence_selected_u[u]
    positive <- rbinom(n_variability, size = 1, prob = p_prev_u) == 1

    raw_gc <- rgamma(
      sum(positive),
      shape = concentration_selected$concentration_gamma_shape[u],
      scale = concentration_selected$positive_mean_gc[u] / concentration_selected$concentration_gamma_shape[u]
    )

    # Convert raw qPCR copies to initial bioavailable infectious virions (Effective GC / Virions)
    infectious_dose_precook_matrix[positive, u] <- raw_gc * q_u[u]
  }
  infectious_dose_precook_matrix
},
    .rng_kind = "Mersenne-Twister", .rng_normal_kind = "Inversion",
    .rng_sample_kind = "Rejection")

module1_uncertainty_inputs <- tibble(
  uncertainty_iteration = seq_len(n_uncertainty),
  prevalence_mean = prevalence_selected_u,
  positive_mean_gc = concentration_selected$positive_mean_gc,
  concentration_gamma_shape = concentration_selected$concentration_gamma_shape,
  q_inv = q_inv_u
)
write_csv(module1_uncertainty_inputs, here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "module1_uncertainty_inputs.csv"))
infectious_dose_precook_node <- mcdata(infectious_dose_precook_matrix, type = "VU")
saveRDS(infectious_dose_precook_node, here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "infectious_dose_precook_node.rds"))

# Calculate per-oyster post-cook residual doses across cooking scenarios and size classes
# calculate_per_oyster_postcook_node is defined in module1_exposure_assessment_thermal_inactivation_functions.R

  # Load survival iteration data from RDS to generate nodes without running simulations
  module2_cooking_scenarios_geeraerd <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_2_thermal_inactivation", "module1_2_cooking_scenarios_geeraerd.rds"))
  survival_fraction_table_geeraerd <- module2_cooking_scenarios_geeraerd$survival_data
  
  module2_cooking_scenarios_meta <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_2_thermal_inactivation", "module1_2_cooking_scenarios_meta.rds"))
  survival_fraction_table_meta <- module2_cooking_scenarios_meta$survival_data

  # convert_survival_to_mc2d_nodes is defined in module1_exposure_assessment_thermal_inactivation_functions.R
  mc2d_survival_nodes_geeraerd <- convert_survival_to_mc2d_nodes(survival_fraction_table_geeraerd, n_unc = n_uncertainty)
  mc2d_survival_nodes_meta <- convert_survival_to_mc2d_nodes(survival_fraction_table_meta, n_unc = n_uncertainty)

# 1. Primary Baseline Model (Geeraerd) - Per-oyster residual dose nodes
  mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd <- map(mc2d_survival_nodes_geeraerd, function(s_node) {
  calculate_per_oyster_postcook_node(infectious_dose_precook_node, s_node)
})
saveRDS(mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd, here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd.rds"))

# 2. Sensitivity Model (Mafart / Meta-Analysis) - Per-oyster residual dose nodes
  mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta <- map(mc2d_survival_nodes_meta, function(s_node) {
  calculate_per_oyster_postcook_node(infectious_dose_precook_node, s_node)
})
saveRDS(mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta, here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta.rds"))

# Scenario Condition Grid for Module 2 risk iteration
condition_grid <- survival_fraction_table_geeraerd %>%
  distinct(method, size, time_min) %>%
  arrange(method, size, time_min)
saveRDS(condition_grid, here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "condition_grid.rds"))

# Export Section 1.3 Pre-Cook & Post-Cook Exposure Assessment Summaries
precook_dose_summary <- tibble(
  metric = c("Mean Precook Dose (Virions/oyster)", "Median Precook Dose", "P95 Precook Dose", "P99 Precook Dose"),
  value = c(
    mean(infectious_dose_precook_matrix),
    median(infectious_dose_precook_matrix),
    quantile(infectious_dose_precook_matrix, 0.95),
    quantile(infectious_dose_precook_matrix, 0.99)
  )
)
write_csv(precook_dose_summary, here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "module1_3_per_oyster_precook_exposure_summary.csv"))

# Per-oyster Post-Cook Exposure Summaries across all cooking conditions
# summarize_postcook_dose_nodes is defined in module1_exposure_assessment_thermal_inactivation_functions.R
postcook_exposure_summary_geeraerd <- summarize_postcook_dose_nodes(mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd)
postcook_exposure_summary_meta <- summarize_postcook_dose_nodes(mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta)
write_csv(postcook_exposure_summary_geeraerd, here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "module1_3_per_oyster_postcook_exposure_summary_geeraerd.csv"))
write_csv(postcook_exposure_summary_meta, here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "module1_3_per_oyster_postcook_exposure_summary_meta.csv"))
```

# Module 2 & 3: Hazard & Risk Characterization

```{r module2-hazard-characterization}
source(here("scripts", "module2_hazard_characterization_functions.R"))
```


## Purpose

Module 2 receives the 2D per-oyster exposure dose matrices from Section 1.3, constructs 12-oyster mixed servings (with post-hoc size mixing across Small, Medium, and Large oysters), and evaluates infection and illness risk per serving.

Dose-response risk is evaluated using the **Teunis et al. (2020)** Kummer hypergeometric dose-response model ($1F1$) parameterized for HuNoV GII ($Se^+$):

$$P_{\text{inf}}(D \mid Se^+) = 1 - {}_1F_1(\alpha, \alpha + \beta, -D)$$
$$P_{\text{ill|inf}}(D \mid Se^+) = 1 - (1 + D / \eta)^{-\rho}$$

Host susceptibility is represented by a Beta distribution fitted to Messner et al. (2014) (mean 0.72, 95% CrI 0.63–0.80):

$$P(Se^+) \sim \operatorname{Beta}(\alpha_{\text{se}}, \beta_{\text{se}})$$

Risk is evaluated for both:
1. **Baseline Primary Model**: Geeraerd model (fitted with 100°C experimental data).
2. **Sensitivity Analysis Model**: Systematic Review Bayesian Meta-Analysis model (Mafart model with shellfish parameters $D_{60} = 4.30\text{ min}, z = 30.10^\circ\text{C}, \beta = 0.39$).

## Risk Evaluation per Serving
```{r module2-teunis-risk-evaluation, eval=FALSE}
source(here("scripts", "module3_risk_characterization_functions.R"))

infectious_dose_precook_node <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "infectious_dose_precook_node.rds"))
mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd.rds"))
mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta  <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta.rds"))
condition_grid <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "condition_grid.rds"))

geeraerd_summary_rds <- here("results", "module3_risk_characterization", "module3_serving_risk_summary_geeraerd.rds")
meta_summary_rds <- here("results", "module3_risk_characterization", "module3_serving_risk_summary_meta.rds")

# 1. Evaluate Baseline Model Risk (Geeraerd)
module4_output_summary_geeraerd <- evaluate_model_risk_summary(
  precook_node = infectious_dose_precook_node,
  postcook_nodes_list = mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd,
  condition_grid = condition_grid,
  n_var = n_variability,
  n_unc = n_uncertainty
)
saveRDS(module4_output_summary_geeraerd, geeraerd_summary_rds)
write_csv(module4_output_summary_geeraerd, here("results", "module3_risk_characterization", "module3_serving_risk_summary_geeraerd.csv"))

# 2. Evaluate Sensitivity Analysis Model Risk (Systematic Review Meta-Analysis / Mafart)
module4_output_summary_meta <- evaluate_model_risk_summary(
  precook_node = infectious_dose_precook_node,
  postcook_nodes_list = mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta,
  condition_grid = condition_grid,
  n_var = n_variability,
  n_unc = n_uncertainty
)
saveRDS(module4_output_summary_meta, meta_summary_rds)
write_csv(module4_output_summary_meta, here("results", "module3_risk_characterization", "module3_serving_risk_summary_meta.csv"))
```

```{r module4-plot-annual-illness-burden}
# Load annual illness summary datasets
module4_us_annual_illness_summary <- read_csv(
  here("results", "module3_risk_characterization", "module3_us_annual_illness_summary.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
module4_us_annual_illness_summary_meta <- read_csv(
  here("results", "module3_risk_characterization", "module3_us_annual_illness_summary_meta.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Using 90% Credible Interval (5th-95th percentile) following CDC/FDA burden reporting conventions
# Prepare plotting data: mixed size, commercial cooked oysters, and raw oyster baseline
plot_annual_illness_burden <- function(summary_df) {
  df_raw <- summary_df %>% filter(method == "raw")
  
  df_bake <- summary_df %>% filter(method == "baking", size == "mixed", time_min > 0) %>%
    bind_rows(df_raw %>% mutate(method = "baking"))
    
  df_steam <- summary_df %>% filter(method == "steaming", size == "mixed", time_min > 0) %>%
    bind_rows(df_raw %>% mutate(method = "steaming"))
    
  df_plot <- bind_rows(df_bake, df_steam) %>%
    mutate(
      serving_size_label = paste(serving_size, "oysters"),
      cooking_time_label = ifelse(time_min == 0, "0 (Raw)", as.character(time_min)),
      method_label = str_to_title(method)
    )
    
  # Order the factors
  df_plot$cooking_time_label <- factor(df_plot$cooking_time_label, levels = c("0 (Raw)", "2", "4", "6", "8", "10", "12", "14", "16"))
  df_plot$method_label <- factor(df_plot$method_label, levels = c("Baking", "Steaming"))
  
  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = cooking_time_label, y = expected_annual_us_illnesses)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "black", fill = "#D55E00") +
    facet_wrap(~method_label, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#EAECEE"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Cooking holding time (minutes)",
      y = "Expected Annual U.S. HuNoV Illnesses"
    )
}

# 1. Primary Geeraerd Plot
p_annual_geeraerd <- plot_annual_illness_burden(module4_us_annual_illness_summary)
ggsave(plot = p_annual_geeraerd, filename = here("figures", "module3_annual_illness_bars_geeraerd.tiff"), width = 10, height = 6)

# 2. Sensitivity Meta-Analysis (Mafart Weibull) Plot
p_annual_meta <- plot_annual_illness_burden(module4_us_annual_illness_summary_meta)
ggsave(plot = p_annual_meta, filename = here("figures", "module3_annual_illness_bars_meta_analysis.tiff"), width = 10, height = 6)
p_annual_geeraerd
p_annual_meta
```

# Module 4: Model Diagnostics and Sensitivity Analysis

## Simulation Numerical Convergence Assessment

```{r module4-simulation-convergence-assessment}
source(here("scripts", "module4_sensitivity_analysis_functions.R"))
infectious_dose_precook_node <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "infectious_dose_precook_node.rds"))

# Assess numerical stability of Mean P(illness) across N_var and N_unc
conv_res <- assess_simulation_convergence(
  precook_node = infectious_dose_precook_node,
  sizes_var = c(500, 1000, 2500, 5000, 10000),
  sizes_unc = c(50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000)
)

# Export Convergence Data
write_csv(conv_res, here("results", "module4_sensitivity_analysis", "module4_numerical_convergence_data.csv"))

# Plot Convergence Curves
plot_simulation_convergence(conv_res, here("figures", "module4_numerical_convergence_plot.tiff"))
```


## Uncertainty Parameter Sensitivity Analysis (Spearman Tornado Plot)

Uncertainty sensitivity analysis was conducted using Spearman rank correlation coefficients ($\rho$) to evaluate the monotonic relationship between primitive uncertain model input parameters and uncertainty-level mean illness probability.

```{r module4-sensitivity-tornado}
mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd.rds"))
mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta  <- readRDS(here("results", "module1_3_exposure_dose_calculation", "mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta.rds"))

# Combined Tornado Plot for Baseline (Geeraerd) and Meta-Analysis Models
plot_combined_tornado_sensitivity(
  postcook_nodes_list_geeraerd = mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd,
  postcook_nodes_list_meta = mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta,
  output_filepath = here("figures", "module4_sensitivity_tornado_p_illness_combined.tiff")
)
```

## Regional Sensitivity Analysis: Monte Carlo Filtering (MCF)

```{r module4-monte-carlo-filtering}
# Run MCF for Geeraerd (Representative Scenario: Steaming Medium 4 min)
mcf_result_geeraerd <- run_monte_carlo_filtering(
  postcook_nodes_list = mc2d_postcook_nodes_geeraerd,
  cutoff = 0.0001,
  model_type = "geeraerd"
)
write_csv(mcf_result_geeraerd$ks_table, here("results", "module4_sensitivity_analysis", "module4_mcf_ks_test_results_geeraerd.csv"))
mcf_result_geeraerd$ks_table
plot_mcf_cdf_curves(mcf_result_geeraerd, here("figures", "module4_mcf_cdf_top_parameters_geeraerd.tiff"))

# Run MCF for Meta-Analysis (Representative Scenario: Steaming Medium 4 min)
mcf_result_meta <- run_monte_carlo_filtering(
  postcook_nodes_list = mc2d_postcook_nodes_meta,
  cutoff = 0.0001,
  model_type = "meta"
)
write_csv(mcf_result_meta$ks_table, here("results", "module4_sensitivity_analysis", "module4_mcf_ks_test_results_meta.csv"))
mcf_result_meta$ks_table
plot_mcf_cdf_curves(mcf_result_meta, here("figures", "module4_mcf_cdf_top_parameters_meta.tiff"))
```
